Jiangxi Copper – China’s biggest and best _page 2_ Since its inception in 1997, Jiangxi Copper Corporation Limited (JCCL) has grown to become the largest producer of refined copper in China and the fifth largest producer worldwide.  JCCL is an integrated copper producer, with operations covering mining, concentrating, smelting, refining and semifabricating.  It is also an important producer of gold, silver, rare metals and sulphuric acid, and will soon become a significant lead and zinc producer once construction of a new smelting complex is completed at end 2011. 

JCCL owns five domestic copper mines – including Dexing, China’s largest – and one lead-zinc mine, accounting for 17% of national copper mine output in 2008.  The company also owns China’s largest smelter-refinery complex – Guixi – accounting for 20% of domestic production of refined copper in 2008.  JCCL is also China’s largest copper semi-fabricator, with six processing plants. 

JCCL, however, is not resting on its laurels and has already expanded refined capacity at its Guixi smelter/refinery complex to 950,000t/y of refined copper this year.  In an attempt to guarantee raw materials, the company plans to expand production at its Dexing copper mine and has invested in two projects outside China – El Galeno in Peru and Aynak in Afghanistan.  Mine production is set to increase to some 200,000t/y of copper in concentrate by 2012. Fabrication capacity is also planned to rise to 680,000t/y.

# Jiangxi Copper – China’s biggest and best 

## Introduction 

Jiangxi Copper Company Limited (JCCL) is the largest producer of refined copper in China and the fifth largest producer worldwide.  Incorporated as a Sino-foreign joint venture joint stock limited company in January 1997, JCCL is 42.41% owned by Jiangxi Copper Corporation (JCC), in turn a 100% state-owned subsidiary of the Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Jiangxi province.  The balance of 57.59% is held by private investors.  JCCL became China’s first mining company to list on a foreign exchange when it issued shares on the Hong Kong and London Stock Exchanges in June 1997, and is now also listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.  It is headquartered in Guixi City in Jiangxi province and had 23,405 employees at end-2008. 

JCCL is an integrated copper producer, with operations covering mining, concentrating, smelting, refining and semi-fabricating.  It is also an important producer of gold, silver, rare metals and sulphuric acid, and in mid-2009, construction began on a lead and zinc smelting complex.  The company’s main products are registered on international exchanges:  copper cathode is registered on the LME and the SHFE, while gold and silver are registered on the LBMA.  Overseas, JCCL has a 25% interest in Aynak copper project in Afghanistan and a 40%

interest in Northern Peru Copper.  This article reviews JCCL’s domestic and overseas copper activities. 

## JCCL’s domestic copper operations 

JCCL is China’s largest copper producer and output rose strongly in 2008, partly in line with expansion projects.  Output of refined copper from the Guixi smelter, the largest in China, increased by 27% to 702,450t in 2008 and accounted for nearly 20% of the national total.  JCCL has risen from eleventh place in the world ranking of refined copper producers in 2006 to fifth position in 2008.  Refining capacity rose to 950,000t/y in 2009 and output of refined copper is scheduled to rise by 8% to 760,000t this year. 

JCCL owns five domestic copper mines – Dexing, the country’s largest open pit mine, Wushan, the largest underground mine, Chengmenshan, Yongping and Dongxiang – as well as Yinshan lead-zinc mine.  Output of copper-in-concentrate increased by 3% to 159,300t in 2008, 17% of national output, and is projected to increase to 167,000t in 2009.  The company’s wholly-owned domestic copper reserves totalled 11.14 million tonnes  of contained Cu at end-2008, and attributable reserves from jointly controlled resources totalled 4.07 million tonnes. 

JCCL is also China’s largest copper semi-fabricator, operating six processing plants – Jiangxi Copper Products, Jiangxi Copper Alloy Materials, Jiangxi Yates Copper Foil, Jiangxi Copper Taiyi Special Electrical Materials, Jiangxi Copper Leongchang Precise Pipe and Jiangxi Copper Corporation Copper Products.  Production capacity totals 500,000t/y.  The main products are copper foil, copper pipe and enamelled wire.  Fabrication capacity is planned to rise to 680,000t/y following expansions in copper sheet and strip and copper foil operations.  Production is targeted to rise from 462,000t in 2008 to 480,000t in 2009. 

Sichuan Kangxi Copper in southwest China and two sulphuric acid plants – JCC Wengfu Chemical and Jiangxi Copper Group Chemical – are also owned by JCCL.  Total sulphuric acid production rose by over 30% from 1.62 million tonnes in 2007 to 2.18 million tonnes in 2008. 

##### JCCL buys out its parent’s assets 

JCCL has been steadily buying out the operational assets of its parent company, Jiangxi Copper Corporation (JCC).  In 2007, it acquired the operating assets and related business of Chengmenshan Copper Mine, a 40% equity interest in both Jiangxi Copper Alloy Materials and Jiangxi Copper Products,

##### Dexing Copper Mine 

Dexing Copper Mine in Dexing City, Jiangxi province, is JCCL’s largest copper mine with proven reserves of 5.9 million tonnes of contained Cu.  It is China’s largest open pit mine and utilises modern equipment such as Komatsu/Euclid/Unit Rig 154t and 176t haulage trucks, P&H electric shovels with 16.8m<sup>3</sup> buckets, Bucyrus 45R rotary blast drills.  There is also a GPS truck dispatch system. 

JCCL’s operations at Dexing mine dominate the area.  Of 10,000 people living in Dexing, 6,000 work at the mine.  Mining has been undertaken in the area since the Tang Dynasty (618-907), whilst large scale open pit operations have been in operation for over 20 years.  The Tang Shan open pit covers around 5.5km<sup>2</sup> and annual production is some 66 million tonnes per year of material (waste and ore).  Ore production is around 90,000t/d, grading 0.4% Cu.  Stripping ratio is 1: 1 (ore:waste) and the mine life is at least 30 years.  Expansion is taking place from the west of the mine. 

Fujiawu open pit is located on the other side of the hill from the older Tang Shan pit.  The mine’s upgrading and expansion project passed environmental review in early 2008.  Fujiawu commenced production in July 2007 with an initial production of 1,000t/d of ore.  This will eventually reach 10,000t/d.  Ore grade at Fujiawu is also around 0.4% Cu.  A 6km conveyor transports ore from Fujiawu to the concentrator.  Fujiawu will increase Dexing’s annual capacity by 22,265t copper-in-concentrate, 80kg gold, 1,988kg silver and 23,855t pyrite concentrate once it reaches full capacity. 

At Tang Shan, there are two primary, gyratory crushers, at the east and west sides of the open pit. Crushed ore is taken from the newer plant on the east side by conveyer belt to the mill.  On the west side ore is transported to the mill by either train or trucks.  The highest-grade ore goes to the mill and then to the concentrator.  Waste rock goes to the dumps while low-grade ores are heap leached.

## Recent financial performance 

At end-December 2008, JCCL’s assets totalled RMB 34,510 million.  Despite the economic downturn in the last quarter of the year, the company’s operating income rose by 29% to RMB 53,201 million in 2008. Net income fell by 45% from RMB 4,133 million in 2007 to RMB 2,285 million in 2008, however, reflecting the fall in product prices in the second half of the year, higher fuel and electricity costs, and increased resource and income tax rates.  Earnings per share were RMB 0.76 in 2008, a drop from RMB 1.40 in 2007. 

For the first half of 2009, JCCL‘s net profit fell by 59% year-on-year to RMB 1.27 billion, compared to RMB 3.08 billion in the first half of 2008.  Earnings per share were RMB 0.42 compared to RMB 1.02.

## JCCL’s products 

##### Copper cathode 

JCCL produced 702,450t of **copper cathode** in 2008.  The cathode is marketed under the _Guiye_ and _Jiangtong_ tradenames and is registered on the LME and SHFE exchanges. 

##### Rare metals 

**Selenium** powder and ingot are used in the pharmaceuticals, chemicals, metallurgy, glass and electronics industries.  JCCL’s product grades ≥99% Se and complies with the YS/T223-1996 specification, with a trademark Se-3, Se≥99%.  Production of selenium products totalled 351t in 2008. 

**Rhenium** powder is used in alloys, the electronics and chemicals industries, and in coating and welding.  It grades ≥99.99% Re and complies with Q/HX06-2000 specification.  Output of ammonium rhenate totalled 2,810kg in 2008. 

**Tellurium** is used a range of high-tech industries including metallurgy, electronics, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, aerospace, national defence, computers, infrared remote sensing

, and military science and technology.  The 1# Te Ingot, grading ≥99.99%, complies with YS/T222-1996 specification, trademark Te-1, while High-Purity Te grades ≥99.999% and complies with Q/HX03-2000 specification.  41t of tellurium concentrate were produced in 2008. 

JCCL also produced 3,106t of standard **molybdenum concentrates** (45% Mo) and 449t of **bismuth concentrat** e in 2008. 

##### Precious metals 

Production of **gold ingot** rose significantly last year, increasing by 24% from 13,192kg in 2007 to 16,300kg in 2008.  Gold ingot is marketed under the _Guiye_ and _Jiangtong_ tradenames.  It complies with

JCCL’s **silver ingot** , grading ≥99.99% and ≥99.95% is also registered on the LBMA and is marketed as _Guiye_ and _Jiangtong._ It meets quality standard GB/T4135-2002.  Production rose by 13% from 360t in 2007 to 408t in 2008. 

##### Chemical products 

**Arsenic trioxide** produced by JCCL meets the YS/T99-1997 quality standard.  It is used mainly in the industrial chemicals, glass, ceramics, nonferrous metals and pharmaceuticals industries.  Production is around 1,400t/y. 

2.18 million tonnes of **sulphuric acid** were produced in 2008.  The sulphuric acid conforms to GB/T534-2002 standard and is used in the chemicals, dyes, agrichemicals, steel, textiles, pharmaceuticals and food industries. 

Some 1.55 million tonnes of **pyrite concentrate** were produced in 2008, a rise from 1.22 million tonnes in 2007.  Around 60% of output comes from Yongping Mine, with smaller quantities produced by Wushan Mine, Dexing Mine, Yinshan Mine and Dongxiang Mine.  The concentrate meets quality standard YS/T337-1998 and is used mainly in sulphate production and the chemicals industries. 

##### Semi-fabricated copper 

##### **Copper wire** 

JCCL produces around 100,000t/y of bare copper wire with a 2.6mm diameter.  It meets quality standard GB/T3953-1983 and is used in products including enamelled wire, and data, video, communication and electric cables. 

##### **Copper wirerod** 

Copper wirerod produced by JCCL meets quality standard GB/T3952-1998.  IN 2008, JCCL produced 411,000 t of 8mm copper wirerod, which is both processed into bare wire in-house and sold. 

##### **Electrolytic copper foil** 

JCCL’s electrolytic copper foil product range includes standard electrolytic (STD-E), high-extension electrolytic (HD-E), high-temperature extension electrolytic (HTE-E), low-outline electrolytic (LP-E) and very low-outline electrolytic (VLP-E) grades.  The products can be produced in a range of finishes, including galvanised and double-sided texture, tailored to customers’ requirements.  The maximum foil width is around 1,295mm, and the foil is produced in thicknesses of 12, 18 and 35μ. 

## Scientific & Research Institute

JCCL’s Technical Centre was established in July 1999. It consists of several departments: the Office (located at the R&D Department), the Mine Department (located at Detong Branch), the Metallurgy & Chemical Engineering Department (located at Guiye Branch) and the Information Department (located at Guiye Branch). The Metallurgy & Chemical Engineering Department has two advanced pilot workshops for mineral processing and the Mine Department has one pilot plant and one experimental leaching plant. ## Developments in China ##### Mine expansions In May 2007, JCC announced that it had signed an agreement with the local government to restructure **Chengmenshan Copper Mine** in Jiujiang county of Jiangxi province. Capacity at the mine, now owned by JCCL, is planned to rise to 7,000t/d of ore; output from the existing facilities is scheduled to rise to 2,000t/d and output from new facilities will add an additional 5,000t/d. ### Jiangxi Copper’s output of Cu in concentrate In July 2007, JCC paid the Jiangxi Provincial Mineral & Survey Bureau RMB 41.88 million for exploration rights to **Zhushahong Copper Mine** , located in Dexing City in Jiangxi province. Preliminary exploration results indicated copper resources of 377,900t contained metal at the mine. In early 2008, JCCL launched a deep-layer exploitation project at the No.5 orebody at **Dongxiang Copper Mine** . After 30 years of mining, Dongxiang Mine’s current copper resources above -235 metres are sufficient for less than six years of mining. Sizeable copper resources remain below -235 metres and above -410 metres, however. With investment of RMB 124 million (US$17.7 million), construction of © 2009 CRU International Limited confidential www.crumonitor.com COPPER STUDIES October 2009 11 the project will be finished within three years. Deep-layer exploitation is expected to start in 2010, raising mine capacity from the current 500t/d to 1,200t/d. The mine's copper-in-concentrate capacity will increase to 3,300t/y from the current 1,700t/y. Mine life is expected to be extended by 20 years. The preliminary design of a 5,000t/d mining and concentrating technology upgrade at JCCL’s **Yinshan Mining** s

ubsidiary was completed in March 2009.  A feasibility study and the design work were undertaken by China Enfi Engineering Corporation.  Yinshan Mining has mined copper-gold ores since the 1990s.  Total investment in the renovation and expansion project at the copper and gold open-cast mine is about RMB 500 million and construction is scheduled to take two years.  On completion, the mine is expected to produce 6,268t of copper-in-concentrate annually, containing 333kg of gold, 5,563kg of silver and 126,380t of pyrite concentrate.  The internal rate of return of the investment is expected to reach 13.23% after completion of the whole project.  The investment pay-back period for this project is calculated to be 8.6 years. 

JCCL announced new copper resources for the No. 5 deposit owned by its subsidiary, **Dongtong Mining Co Ltd** in mid-2009.  The new resources contain 7.95 million tonnes of ore reserves containing 84,100 tonnes of copper.  Total resources of lines 43-71 in No. 5 deposit amount to 9.37 million tonnes of ore reserves containing 108,500 tonnes of copper. 

##### JCCL’s anode joint venture 

Jiangxi Copper EPI (Qingyuan) Limited was established in November 2006 as a joint venture between JCCL (40%), EPI Metals Limited (51%) and Qingyuan Tongde Electric Industrial Co Ltd (9%).  EPI Metals raised its share to 60% in September 2008.  The joint venture began production in Qingyuan City 70km north of Canton in Guangdong province, one of China’s main recycling areas, in June 2007. Smelting capacity was 100,000t/y, divided equally between capacity to smelt concentrates into blister and capacity to smelt scrap into anode.  Initially, capacity was expected to double to 200,000t/y.  All output is supplied to JCCL. 

Between June and December 2007, 24,457t of copper anode were produced.  In 2008, just 30,375t of copper anode and 1,827t of copper scrap were supplied to JCCL, as plant operations suffered from heavy snowfall and flooding in the first half of the year, and from raw material shortages towards the end of the year.  As margins on copper anode production remain low in 2009, the company plans to increase supplies of copper scrap to JCCL rather than processing more copper anode this year. 

##### Diversification into lead and zinc 

JCCL started construction of its lead and zinc smelting project in Jiujiang, Jiangxi province in late June 2009.  Phase 1 of the project, involving investment of RMB 2.8 billion, aims to produce 100,000t/y of electrolytic lead using the Kivcet process and 100,000t/y of electrolytic zinc using the hydrometallurgical process.  It is scheduled to come on-stream in Q4 2011.  Phase 2 of the project involves raising lead and zinc smelting capacity to 200,000t/y each.  The timetable for Phase 2 has not yet been decided.  Once the whole project is completed, it will also have capacity to produce 560,000t/y of sulphuric acid, 2t/y of gold, 182t/y of silver, 1,290t/y of cadmium, 13.7t/y of indium and 7,270t/y of copper

matte. JCC expects the project to add RMB 6.8 billion to its annual revenue and RMB 740 million to annual profits. JCC entered an agreement with the provincial government to develop lead and zinc resources. In November 2007, the company signed a cooperation agreement with Jiangxi Bureau of Geology and Mineral Resources, to jointly exploit lead and zinc resources in Jiangxi province. A new company was established in the first half of 2008 to operate the lead and zinc mines, concentrators and a smelter in Jiangxi. Three lead and zinc mines are located in Guixi Lengshuikeng Mining Area and one at De'an Zhangshiba. ## Investment outside China 

JCCL has spent around RMB 2.5 billion on acquiring North Peru Copper Corp and Afghanistan Aynak Copper.  These have added around 16 million tonnes to the company’s copper reserves.  JCCL bought the assets with its latest issue of warrants and convertible bonds totalling RMB 13.6 billion.  North Peru Copper has at least 3.3 million tonnes of contained Cu resources and Aynak Copper has 13 million tonnes of contained Cu reserves. 

##### Large reserves in Afghanistan 

In November 2007, JCCL, together with China Metallurgical Group and Fujian Zijin Mining Co Ltd, won the rights to develop a large copper deposit in Afghanistan.  The copper deposit is 35km southeast of Kabul, the capital of Afghanistan.  It was discovered in 1974 and explored by Soviet geologists in 1978, who identified 705 million tonnes of ore at 1.26% Cu, but the deposit has never been developed due to years of civil war.  The record foreign investment of US$2.87 billion is expected to generate employment for 100,000 workers at the mine.  Reserves are currently estimated at 13 million tonnes, but could increase to 20 million tonnes, making Aynak the second largest unexploited deposit worldwide. Production is scheduled to reach 300,000t/y of copper in concentrate. 

MCC Jiangtong Aynak Mining Co Ltd officially took over the mining rights on Aynak copper mine from the Afghanistan government on 25<sup>th</sup> November 2008.  MCC Jiangtong Aynak Mining is a joint venture between JCCL (25%) and China Metallurgical Group (75%).  The joint venture will be responsible for constructing and operating Aynak copper mine. 

Construction of the project began in July 2009 with demining (location and removal of landlines) a prerequisite for any further development.  Landmine Impact Assessment Teams deployed by the Afghan government found that some 4.135km<sup>2</sup> of land around the Aynak area is contaminated with landmines and 1.4km2 is contaminated with Explosive Remnants of War. (ammunition, tanks and other weapons). Demining operations will last for 18 months and are due to be completed in December 2010. 

The initial capacity (Phase 1) will be some 200,000t/y of copper in concentrate.  The plan is to expand the operation to 1.03 million tonnes of copper concentrate (29% Cu) yielding 300,000t/y of copper in
